what_its_for: Alcohol antiseptic is used to kill germs, bacteria, and some viruses on your skin. It helps prevent the spread of infection. It is commonly used to clean your hands, prepare your skin before a shot or blood draw, or clean minor cuts and scrapes.
how_to_take: For hand sanitizer: Apply enough gel or liquid to cover the palm of one hand. Rub your hands together, covering all surfaces including between fingers and around your nails, until your hands feel dry (about 20–30 seconds). Do NOT rinse off. For skin prep or wound cleaning: Apply a small amount to a cotton ball, swab, or gauze pad and gently wipe the skin area. Let the skin air dry before any injection or procedure. Do NOT swallow or use inside your mouth, eyes, ears, or deep wounds.
dosing: Use as needed throughout the day for hand hygiene, especially before eating, after using the restroom, after blowing your nose, coughing, or sneezing, and after touching surfaces in public places. For skin preparation before injections: use once per site just before the procedure. There is no strict dose limit for external use, but avoid excessive or repeated use that causes skin irritation.
missed_dose: Alcohol antiseptic is used as needed and does not have a scheduled dosing routine. Simply use it the next time you need to clean your hands or prepare your skin. There is no 'missed dose' concern with this product.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C–30°C). Keep the cap tightly closed when not in use to prevent evaporation. Keep away from heat, open flames, and sparks — alcohol is flammable. Store out of reach of children. Do not store in direct sunlight or in your car on hot days. Check the expiration date and do not use if expired, as the product may be less effective.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT swallow alcohol antiseptic — it can cause serious poisoning, especially in children. Do NOT use near open flames, while smoking, or near heat sources, as alcohol is highly flammable. Do NOT apply to large open wounds, deep cuts, or burned skin. Do NOT get in your eyes, ears, or mouth. Do NOT rely on hand sanitizer if your hands are visibly dirty or greasy — wash with soap and water instead. Do NOT use on children's hands and then allow them to put their hands in their mouths before the product has fully dried.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek medical help if: someone swallows alcohol antiseptic (call Poison Control immediately at 1-800-222-1222); you develop a skin rash, severe redness, swelling, or blistering after use; you have an allergic reaction such as hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the face or throat; a wound you cleaned with alcohol shows signs of worsening infection such as increasing redness, warmth, pus, or fever.
when_it_works: Alcohol antiseptic works very quickly — it starts killing germs within seconds of being applied to the skin. It is most effective when used properly (enough product, rubbed in completely until dry). Keep in mind it does NOT remove all types of germs (such as norovirus or C. difficile spores), and it works best when hands are not visibly soiled.
special_populations: Children: Keep hand sanitizers out of reach of young children. A small amount can cause alcohol poisoning if swallowed. Use only with adult supervision. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: External use is generally considered safe. Avoid swallowing. Elderly: Safe for external use. Be aware that frequent use may cause more skin dryness in older adults — use a moisturizer if needed. People with sensitive skin: Some formulations contain fragrances or other additives that may irritate sensitive skin. Choose fragrance-free options if needed.
